title: evidence-snapshot-orchestrator-for-temporal-retention-and-signer-chains
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Objective: build an orchestrator that snapshots control evidence across region-bound stores, applies retention policy metadata, and produces tamper-evident signed artifacts auditors can replay. This ticket scopes the product requirements, high-level design constraints, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the first MVP.

Background: customers are asking for an auditable export that demonstrates adherence to SOC 2/ISO controls for data residency and retention. Current artifacts are scattered (S3 exports, DB snapshots, Console logs) and lack standardized signing, sequencing, and retention metadata, which slows audits and raises compliance risk.

MVP scope:
- Periodic snapshot job that captures a named set of telemetry and control proofs (access logs, policy evaluation results, configuration manifests, encryption key rotation events) for a given tenant and region.
- Attach canonical metadata: retention policy id, region, data residency claim, snapshot window, and TTL.
- Produce a chained signature (signer chain) per snapshot to prove sequence and integrity; include key fingerprints and signing timestamps.
- Export format: newline-delimited JSON with a small JSON-LD header (versioned) and compressed payload (.ndjson.gz).
- Auditor playback: lightweight CLI that consumes the artifact, verifies signature chain, and produces a compact report mapping artifacts to SOC 2/ISO controls.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Sample artifact created for one enterprise tenant in eu-west with at least 3 evidence types (access log slice, config manifest, policy-eval snapshot).
2) Artifacts include retention metadata and TTL equal to customer policy and can be queried by retention window.
3) Signer chain validated by CLI and by Console verification UI.
4) Integration tests (unit + e2e) demonstrating replay flow and control mapping for 5 control IDs.
5) Documentation (Confluence) and auditor-runbook ready.

Design trade-offs and decisions:
- Use existing evidence-collector microservice to source raw items to speed iteration (trade-off: initial artifacts may lack schema normalization; normalization layer added in next sprint).
- Signer chain uses HSM-backed signing in Dedicated/Private; hosted customers use KMS envelope signing with recorded key fingerprint.
- Export format chosen for simple streaming consumption; alternative (zip/one-file JSON blob) rejected because it complicates streaming validation and memory usage.

Integrations and telemetry:
- Hook into Console export workflow and provide per-tenant export history.
- Emit telemetry for snapshot size, generation latency, sign latency, and verification success rate; surface in compliance dashboard.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (MVP): single-tenant exports, CLI verifier, Confluence runbook, internal security review.
- Phase 2: multi-tenant queued exports, retention policy enforcement, auditor role and temporary access tokens, role-based downloads for SSO customers.
- Phase 3: add proof-of-custody ledger and long-term archive lifecycle hooks.

Links and artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Evidence+Snapshot+Orchestrator
- Design spec (draft): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1X-SNAPSHOT-DESIGN
- Sample artifact (proto): https://storage.redwood.ai/snapshots/samples/pm-847263-example.ndjson.gz
- GitHub draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12894
- Compliance dashboard mock: https://console.redwood.ai/compliance/preview/847263

Notes for engineering: include retention enforcement at export generation time, not only at storage TTL. Ensure signer metadata includes KMS key id and signing algorithm. Ensure region tag is immutable in the artifact header.
